parts.visual:
A founder needs money. They can ask a rich dentist (Angel Investor) or a massive Wall Street firm (Venture Capitalist). 

The Players:
1. Angel Investors: High-net-worth individuals who invest their own personal money. They write smaller checks ($25k - $100k) very early on. They are flexible and fast.
2. Venture Capitalists (VCs): Professional firms that invest other people's money. They write massive checks ($2M - $50M). They are ruthless, slow, and demand Board seats and control.
parts.audio: Understanding the difference between an Angel Investor and a Venture Capitalist is critical. Angels invest their own money based on emotion and belief. VCs invest institutional money based on pure mathematics.

questions.question: You just thought of a great idea yesterday. You have no product and no customers. You need $50,000 to build the prototype. Who should you pitch?
options: An Angel Investor (or Friends & Family). VCs generally do not invest in 'ideas'—they invest in traction. Angels are willing to take massive risks on an unproven founder because it's their personal money.
questions.correct_answer: An Angel Investor (or Friends & Family). VCs generally do not invest in 'ideas'—they invest in traction. Angels are willing to take massive risks on an unproven founder because it's their personal money.
questions.explanation: Angels invest in the person. VCs invest in the spreadsheet.

questions.question: Listen to the VC firm's rejection. Why did they pass on the deal despite liking the company?
questions.tts_text: We love the product. We think you will make $10 Million a year. But our minimum check size is $20 Million. Your company is simply too small for our fund economics. We have to pass.
options: Fund Mathematics. Massive VC funds literally cannot write small checks because managing 500 tiny companies is impossible. They are forced to deploy massive amounts of capital into a few huge bets.
Because they ran out of money.
questions.correct_answer: Fund Mathematics. Massive VC funds literally cannot write small checks because managing 500 tiny companies is impossible. They are forced to deploy massive amounts of capital into a few huge bets.
questions.explanation: If a VC fund is $1 Billion, a $50k check doesn't move the needle. They only want to write $20M checks.

questions.question: What is a 'Syndicate' in the context of Angel Investing?
options: A group of 10 or 20 Angel Investors who pool their money together under one lead investor. This allows them to write a massive $1M check combined, acting like a mini-VC.
questions.correct_answer: A group of 10 or 20 Angel Investors who pool their money together under one lead investor. This allows them to write a massive $1M check combined, acting like a mini-VC.
questions.explanation: Syndicates are incredibly powerful because they combine the flexibility of Angels with the capital of VCs.

questions.question: Why do VCs almost always demand a 'Board Seat' when they invest?
options: Because they are investing millions of dollars of other people's money. A Board Seat gives them legal power to fire the CEO if the company starts failing, protecting their investment.
questions.correct_answer: Because they are investing millions of dollars of other people's money. A Board Seat gives them legal power to fire the CEO if the company starts failing, protecting their investment.
questions.explanation: When you take VC money, you are selling a piece of your control.
